title: Honest Conversations About AI in Film Often Feel Impossible. IndieWire and Andreessen Horowitz Tried Anyway
excerpt: IndieWire published video from its Cannes event with a16z, where filmmakers and technologists debated where generative tools actually fit in production. The framing: look at the future without pretending human authorship is optional.
rationale: Filmmakers and toolmakers arguing on the record about where generative tools belong in a real production plan — the production-practice piece the section was missing.

title: Snapchat Banning Entirely AI-Generated Videos From Its Spotlight Platform
excerpt: Snap is barring fully AI-generated videos from Spotlight, its short-form discovery surface, while still allowing creators to use AI to edit or enhance footage. It draws a distribution-level line between AI-assisted craft and wholly synthetic output.
rationale: A distribution platform drawing a hard line between AI-assisted and fully synthetic video sets a rule creators must design their pipeline around, not just an opinion.

title: SeedDance 2.5 Just Got Upstaged by Nvidia
excerpt: Curious Refuge stress-tests the freshly launched Seedance 2.5 against Nvidia's newest generative video work, comparing shot control, motion coherence and where each model breaks down for narrative filmmaking.
rationale: A hands-on head-to-head on shot control and motion coherence is the fastest way to decide which video model to actually spend credits on this week.

title: Tech Reviews: Blender 5, Silhouette 2026 and DaVinci Resolve 21
excerpt: Animation Magazine's monthly software review covers Blender 5, Boris FX's Silhouette 2026 and DaVinci Resolve 21 — with Silhouette's machine-learning roto, matting and paint tooling the headline for compositors.
rationale: Three core post tools reviewed at once, with ML roto and matting as the practical headline — direct, desk-level impact for compositors and editors.

title: Venice-Set Reply AI Film Festival Unveils Finalists & Jury
excerpt: Deadline details the Reply AI Film Festival's finalist shorts and its jury led by Gabriele Salvatores, with Catherine Hardwicke and Jed Weintrob. Winners are announced on the Lido during the Venice Film Festival.
rationale: Mainstream directors judging AI-made shorts on the Lido marks a real distribution and legitimization path for generative filmmakers, not just discourse.
